security_audit.summary: All 82 static findings are false positives. Markdown backticks and prose examples were misclassified as command or reconnaissance activity, while the included Bash validator performs local, quoted text extraction. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Continue quoting the path in every command and consider adding -- before file operands for utilities that support it.

content.value_statement: Plugin agents need clear triggers, bounded tools, and predictable output. This skill provides templates, validation guidance, and examples for building them.
actual_capabilities: Explains agent Markdown files with YAML frontmatter.
Defines specific triggering conditions with usage examples.
Guides system prompts with responsibilities, process, and output format.
Recommends least-privilege tool access for agents.
Shows agent naming, organization, and namespacing patterns.
Provides a Bash validator for agent file structure.
limitations: It does not install, deploy, or register agents automatically.
The validator checks structure and simple content rules only.
It cannot guarantee that an agent triggers correctly in every conversation.
It does not replace project-specific security review or testing.

use_cases.title: Create a first plugin agent
use_cases.description: Build a focused agent file with valid frontmatter, examples, and a structured system prompt.

use_cases.title: Standardize an agent library
use_cases.description: Apply consistent names, tool restrictions, and output expectations across several agents.

use_cases.title: Review agent configuration
use_cases.description: Check triggering descriptions and least-privilege tool choices before testing an agent.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: create an agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-only code review agent for my plugin. Include valid frontmatter, two triggering examples, and a concise output format.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: improve triggers
prompt_templates.scenario: Make an existing agent easier to invoke.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this agent description. Add specific triggering conditions, two realistic examples, and clear cases where the agent should not run.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: restrict tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an agent for generating unit tests. Recommend the minimum tools it needs and explain why each tool is required.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: validate a portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these plugin agent files for naming, frontmatter, triggering examples, tool scope, and system prompt structure. Return prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a documentation agent for API changes.
output: Triggers: API additions, changed endpoints, and documentation requests
Output: updated documentation and a concise change summary

output_examples.input: Review the tools for a code review agent.
output: Keep Read and Grep for analysis.
Do not grant Write unless fixes are requested.
Do not grant Bash unless repository commands are necessary.
Check frontmatter fields and name format.
Confirm triggering examples and system prompt structure.

best_practices: Use specific triggering examples that reflect real user requests.
Grant only the tools needed for the agent task.
Test normal requests and edge cases before publishing an agent.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic descriptions that match unrelated requests.
Do not give every agent unrestricted tool access.
Do not omit the expected output format from the system prompt.

faq.question: What is an agent in this skill?
faq.answer: An agent is a Markdown configuration that defines a specialized autonomous subprocess for a plugin.

faq.question: How does an agent trigger?
faq.answer: Claude uses the description and its examples to decide when the agent matches a request.

faq.question: Which model should I choose?
faq.answer: Use inherit unless the task has a clear need for a specific model.

faq.question: Should every agent receive all tools?
faq.answer: No. Restrict tools to the minimum set required for the task.

faq.question: What does the validator check?
faq.answer: It checks frontmatter, required fields, formats, prompt presence, and basic content guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill test production behavior?
faq.answer: No. You must test triggering and task quality with realistic project scenarios.
